judgments.reasoning_cat1: Descriptive discussion of foreclosure remedies and fraudulent-conveyance risk; 'generally is a remedy alternative to foreclosure' is hedged but the passage is explanatory, not operative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with c151 and c153's treatment of collateral risk; no operative provision on remedies conflicts with it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A Project will be released as collateral as it is sold and the payment is made on the Portfolio Loan' states a release mechanic in a risk factor without saying what payment suffices.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No operative provision anywhere in the Memorandum governs collateral release on cross-collateralised loans, so this risk factor is the only statement of the mechanic — a gap rather than a contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Adequate insurance coverage' is soft, but the paragraph is candid risk disclosure rather than a promise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c069's escrow condition requires fire and casualty insurance naming the Company as loss payee in the amount of the loan, whereas this risk factor describes only liability and property-damage cover the Company 'intends to require' — the two describe the insurance requirement differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long, heavily conditioned mezzanine-risk narrative; 'the Company may seek an inter-creditor agreement' creates no obligation and the (a)/(b) expectations are expressly contingent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It uses 'Other Sponsored Funds' where c055 defined 'Other Sponsored Investment Funds', and contemplates raising capital 'from Noteholders or new investors' to buy senior notes, which presses against the final-closing limit in c099.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear description of the consequences of foreclosing an equity pledge; nothing genuinely ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contemplates Portfolio Loans secured by equity pledges rather than deeds of trust, which sits against c060's statement that the Company makes loans 'secured by deeds of trust' and c062's first-lien expectation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Commercially reasonable efforts in reliance on qualified advisors, including its affiliate Bar-K, Inc.' treats an affiliate as the source of compliance advice, but the wording is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates c133's compliance undertaking in different words; both are disclosure rather than covenant, so no operative conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and hedged ('is expected to comply', 'reasonable efforts'); nothing with two competing readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It repeats c132's usury discussion but addresses only the Portfolio Loans, omitting the usury exposure c132 identifies on the Notes themselves — the same subject covered twice with different scope.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Introductory conflicts paragraph with an expressly non-exhaustive list ('include, but are not limited to'); descriptive only.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c049 says the following is 'a list of the important areas' of conflict and states there are no other contemplated transactions, a closed framing that sits against this open one.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard time-allocation conflict disclosure; nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c056 and c110; the only friction is the different formulations of the time commitment across those provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The heading 'Proportionally Disproportionate Interest' is self-contradictory on its face, and 'Company gains and certain other income' is undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c098 says the Manager will contribute only $25,000 as a Member, and c112 allocates all tax items to Members, so the disproportion described here is real but consistent with the structure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Various potential and actual conflicts ... including, but not limited to' is an open catch-all, and the closing sentence requires the investor to 'entrust all aspects' of management — a sweeping formulation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers to Section III Conflicts of Interest, which c049 frames as a closed list; the two characterisations of the same conflicts are inconsistent in scope.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An introductory sentence framing the Notes as subject to 'risks that are typical of investments in private equity funds'; descriptive only.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Characterising a debt investment by reference to private equity risk sits oddly against c018 and c123's insistence that Noteholders hold debt, not equity, though the point is presentational.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Plain statement of no operating history; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contradicts nothing operative and is the counterweight to the promotional recitals in c022–c025.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Concentration risk disclosure; no operative term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c077's 20% single-loan diversification limit applies only 'after the second year of the Company's term', which is what makes this concentration risk real; the two are complementary.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Blind-pool disclosure with no operative content; nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c060's lending criteria and c015's absence of a capital target.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It concedes that the security 'may be subordinated' and that there is 'no assurance that the Noteholders' security interest will be perfected in seniority', which is candid but leaves the value of the security undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This is the sharpest statement of the tension with c012/c018's promise that 'the Notes will be secured by the assets of the Company' and with c108's advance subordination agreement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence; 'severely restricted' is imprecise but it merely points to the operative restrictions elsewhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c107 permits transfers to family trusts, wholly-owned affiliates and by operation of law, so 'severely restricted' is a summary rather than a conflicting rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Noteholders will bear the economic risks of their investment until the Notes are paid in full' is definite; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c017 and c094 allow discretionary prepayment on request after the Minimum Holding Period, which qualifies 'until the Notes are paid in full' only trivially.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: States flatly that Noteholders cannot participate or vote on Company operating matters; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is in tension with c109's Restricted Actions, which do require Majority in Interest approval of Noteholders for mergers, liens and the Manager's withdrawal, and with c114's amendment consents.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Some portion of his business time' uses a singular pronoun for plural Principals, but the substance is clear disclosure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says decisions 'will be made by the Principals' while c084 vests investment decisions in the Manager and c109 reserves certain actions to Noteholder approval; the actor differs across provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A grab-bag of tax, lending-law and ERISA warnings; entirely hedged and non-operative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers accurately to Section VI and duplicates c132–c134; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It defines the Investment Company Act as 'the Company Act', and the final sentence ('Neither the Company nor its counsel can assure investors that ... the Company may not become subject') is a double negative that inverts the intended meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c003 calls the same statute the 'Investment Company Act' and c130 uses that term too, so the instrument gives one statute three labels; c003's flat 'the Company will not be registered' is also stronger than the mere 'belief' stated here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Closing disclaimer that investors should be able to afford total loss; the reference to a 'favorable track record with making loans similar to those targeted' is puffery inside a disclaimer.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That track-record clause pulls against c026's insistence that past results were historical only and that the Company has no operating history — a recital-versus-warning tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Certain eligibility and suitability standards' is left to the Subscription Agreement, and it introduces 'Interest Roll-over Request' as a capitalised term the Memorandum never defines.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c089 defines 'Roll-over Interest' and describes the request procedure without calling it an 'Interest Roll-over Request'; the requirement to re-qualify at the time of each request is consistent with c091 and c092.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clean lead-in tying the representation to Rule 501 and requiring only one of the following to be true.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c088's definition of Noteholders by reference to accredited-investor status.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Tracks the Rule 501 individual tests, though 'has a reasonable expectation of reaching the same income level in the current year' is attached only to the income prongs and 'the same income level' is ambiguous between the $200,000 and $300,000 figures.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c088 and c173; nothing elsewhere sets a different individual threshold.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It confines the trust category to an 'IRREVOCABLE TRUST', which is narrower than Rule 501, and it ends with a full stop rather than the 'or' used to join the other clauses.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c179 separately qualifies 'a living trust or other revocable trust' whose grantors and trustees are accredited, so revocable trusts are admitted by clause (vi) but excluded by clause (ii) — the two clauses cut against each other.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It refers to an investment company 'registered under the United States Companies Act of 1940', misnaming the Investment Company Act and defining it as 'the Companies Act'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c003 defines the same statute as the 'Investment Company Act' and c170 as the 'Company Act'; three inconsistent labels for one statute in one instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The (A)/(B) structure is ambiguous — the self-directed-plan proviso could attach to (B) alone or to the whole clause — and 'gither' is a typographical error for 'either'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with the ERISA discussion in c128–c129, which addresses Plan Investors without imposing a different asset test.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Not formed for the purpose of acquiring the Note' qualifies the entity types, but the placement of 'in each case with total assets in excess of $5,000,000' leaves it unclear whether the 501(c)(3) organisation is also subject to the 'not formed for the purpose' limit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c180 expressly contemplates 'an entity that was formed for the purpose of purchasing a Note' and admits it if its beneficial owners qualify, which is the opposite of this clause's exclusion.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause qualifies an entity whose owners qualify under 'clause (i), (ii), (iii), (iv) or (v) above or this clause (vi)' — a self-referential definition that can recurse without limit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It admits revocable and living trusts that c175's irrevocable-trust clause excludes, so the two accredited-investor routes are inconsistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short look-through requirement; 'each of its beneficial owners meets one of the criteria' is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It permits entities 'formed for the purpose of purchasing a Note' subject to a look-through, while c178 excludes entities 'not formed for the purpose of acquiring the Note' from that category — a direct tension between paragraphs 1(v) and 2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard investment-intent representation with a trustee carve-out; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c004, c107 and c166's transfer restrictions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Such knowledge and experience ... capable of evaluating the merits and risks' is the standard sophistication formula, applied to the investor rather than a purchaser representative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates the sophistication language in c175 for trusts; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Absolute discretion to accept or reject 'all or a portion' of a subscription, stated without qualification; clear even if one-sided.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c005, c088 and c091; the same discretion is stated in each.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Prior to the closing of the offering' is imprecise where the Memorandum contemplates multiple closings, and 'without unreasonable effort or expense' is the usual soft limit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c099 contemplates an initial closing plus additional closings up to a final closing, so 'the closing of the offering' has no single referent; c007 states the same access right in different words.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It refers to 'the Company and its Managing Member', a term the Memorandum never defines and which conflicts with 'Manager' and 'Members' used throughout.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c081 qualifies the summaries by reference to the Subscription Agreement, Note Purchase Agreement and Company Agreement, and c009 by reference to five Offering Documents, whereas this provision qualifies the Summary of Principal Terms 'in its entirety by reference to the Note Purchase Agreement' alone.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Contact details only; nothing capable of construction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c184's instruction to direct questions to the Principals.
